info.text:
A $600 TV can cost you $1,300.
For example: $20 a week for 65 weeks = $1,300 (our math). You own it only after the last payment.
Same $600 on a card at 22.36% APR (Fed, Q3 2026) over 15 months: about $693 (our math).
A 2017 NerdWallet/Raycom study estimated Rent-A-Center's implied APRs at 43% to 468%.
Rules vary by state: California caps total cost at 2.25x the cash price, Vermont at 2x.
Sources: Federal Reserve G.19, NerdWallet/Raycom (2017), California Civil Code 1812.644, APRO.
News and education, not financial advice.
